Employee.title: Employee
Employee.description: Represents an employee within the GeoHRM system, including their personal details, contact information, and HR-related data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Employee entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the employee.

lastName.description: The last name of the employee.

email.description: The primary email address of the employee, used for communication and identification. (format: email)

dateOfBirth.description: The employee's date of birth. (format: date)

hireDate.description: The date the employee was hired. (format: date)

employeeIdNumber.description: An internal, HR-assigned identification number for the employee.

contactNumber.description: The employee's primary contact phone number.

roleId.description: Reference to the Role assigned to the employee. (Relationship: Role 1:N Employee)

teamLeadId.description: Reference to the Employee who is this employee's direct team lead. Nullable for top-level employees. (Relationship: Employee 1:N Employee)

Role.title: Role
Role.description: Defines a user role within the GeoHRM system, dictating permissions and access levels.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Role entity.

name.description: The descriptive name of the role (e.g., Member, Team Lead, HR Manager, CEO/Admin).

description.description: A detailed explanation of the role's responsibilities and typical permissions.

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Represents a pre-approved physical location for attendance clock-ins, defined by geographical coordinates and a geofence radius.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Location entity.

name.description: A human-readable name for the location (e.g., Main Office, Branch A).

address.description: The physical street address of the location.

latitude.description: The geographical latitude of the location's center point.

longitude.description: The geographical longitude of the location's center point.

radius.description: The radius in meters defining the geofence around the latitude/longitude for attendance verification.

description.description: An optional description or notes about the location.

AttendanceRecord.title: AttendanceRecord
AttendanceRecord.description: Records an employee's daily attendance, including check-in/out times, GPS coordinates, break information, and any admin overrides.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AttendanceRecord entity.

employeeId.description: Reference to the Employee whose attendance this record belongs to. (Relationship: Employee 1:N AttendanceRecord)

checkInTime.description: The timestamp when the employee checked in. (format: date-time)

checkOutTime.description: The timestamp when the employee checked out. Null if still clocked in. (format: date-time)

checkInLatitude.description: The geographical latitude recorded at check-in.

checkInLongitude.description: The geographical longitude recorded at check-in.

checkOutLatitude.description: The geographical latitude recorded at check-out.

checkOutLongitude.description: The geographical longitude recorded at check-out.

approvedLocationId.description: Reference to the approved Location associated with this attendance record. (Relationship: Location 1:N AttendanceRecord)

isWithinApprovedLocation.description: Indicates if the check-in GPS coordinates were within the approved location's geofence.

mislocationReason.description: A reason provided if the check-in was outside the approved location.

status.description: The current status of the attendance record (e.g., 'Present', 'Approved Override', 'Pending Approval').

adminOverrideReason.description: The mandatory reason provided by an administrator for any manual adjustments.

adminOverrideByEmployeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who performed the administrative override. (Relationship: Employee 1:N AttendanceRecord)

adminOverrideTimestamp.description: The timestamp when the administrative override occurred. (format: date-time)

BreakRecord.title: BreakRecord
BreakRecord.description: Details individual breaks taken by an employee during an attendance session.

id.description: Unique identifier for the BreakRecord entity.

attendanceRecordId.description: Reference to the AttendanceRecord this break belongs to. (Relationship: AttendanceRecord 1:N BreakRecord)

breakStartTime.description: The timestamp when the break started. (format: date-time)

breakEndTime.description: The timestamp when the break ended. Null if the break is ongoing. (format: date-time)

description.description: An optional description or notes about the break.

LeaveType.title: LeaveType
LeaveType.description: Defines different categories of leave that employees can request, along with associated policies.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LeaveType entity.

name.description: The name of the leave type (e.g., 'Sick Leave', 'Annual Leave').

description.description: A detailed description of the leave type and its rules.

maxDaysPerYear.description: The maximum number of days allowed for this leave type per year. Null if unlimited.

isPaid.description: Indicates whether this leave type is paid.

LeaveRequest.title: LeaveRequest
LeaveRequest.description: Records an employee's request for leave, including dates, reason, and current approval status within the hierarchical workflow.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LeaveRequest entity.

employeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who submitted the leave request. (Relationship: Employee 1:N LeaveRequest)

leaveTypeId.description: Reference to the LeaveType being requested. (Relationship: LeaveType 1:N LeaveRequest)

startDate.description: The start date of the requested leave. (format: date)

endDate.description: The end date of the requested leave. (format: date)

reason.description: The employee's reason for requesting leave.

status.description: The current status of the leave request (e.g., 'Pending Team Lead Approval', 'Approved', 'Rejected').

requestedDate.description: The timestamp when the leave request was submitted. (format: date-time)

totalDays.description: The calculated total number of leave days requested.

LeaveApproval.title: LeaveApproval
LeaveApproval.description: Records each step of the hierarchical approval process for a LeaveRequest.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LeaveApproval entity.

leaveRequestId.description: Reference to the LeaveRequest being approved. (Relationship: LeaveRequest 1:N LeaveApproval)

approverEmployeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who acted as the approver for this step. (Relationship: Employee 1:N LeaveApproval)

approverRole.description: The role of the approver (e.g., 'Team Lead', 'HR Manager', 'CEO/Admin').

status.description: The outcome of this approval step ('Approved', 'Rejected', 'Pending').

approvalDate.description: The timestamp when this approval step was acted upon. (format: date-time)

notes.description: Any notes or comments provided by the approver.

EmployeeLeaveBalance.title: EmployeeLeaveBalance
EmployeeLeaveBalance.description: Tracks the current leave balance for an employee for a specific leave type and year.

id.description: Unique identifier for the EmployeeLeaveBalance entity.

employeeId.description: Reference to the Employee. (Relationship: Employee 1:N EmployeeLeaveBalance)

leaveTypeId.description: Reference to the LeaveType this balance applies to. (Relationship: LeaveType 1:N EmployeeLeaveBalance)

balanceDays.description: The remaining number of leave days for the employee for this leave type and year.

accruedDays.description: The number of leave days accrued by the employee for this leave type in the current year.

year.description: The calendar year for which this leave balance applies.

IssueCategory.title: IssueCategory
IssueCategory.description: Defines different categories for issue reports, helping to organize and direct reported issues.

id.description: Unique identifier for the IssueCategory entity.

name.description: The name of the issue category (e.g., 'IT Support', 'Facility Maintenance').

description.description: A detailed description of what types of issues fall under this category.

IssueReport.title: IssueReport
IssueReport.description: Records non-emergency issues reported by staff, including their status and assignment details.

id.description: Unique identifier for the IssueReport entity.

reporterEmployeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who submitted the issue report. (Relationship: Employee 1:N IssueReport)

issueCategoryId.description: Reference to the IssueCategory this report belongs to. (Relationship: IssueCategory 1:N IssueReport)

title.description: A concise title for the issue.

description.description: A detailed description of the reported issue.

reportDate.description: The timestamp when the issue was reported. (format: date-time)

status.description: The current status of the issue (e.g., 'New', 'Assigned', 'Resolved').

assignedToEmployeeId.description: Reference to the Employee assigned to resolve the issue. Null if unassigned. (Relationship: Employee 1:N IssueReport)

resolutionNotes.description: Notes documenting the resolution steps or outcome of the issue.

lastUpdatedDate.description: The timestamp of the last update to the issue report. (format: date-time)

Announcement.title: Announcement
Announcement.description: Stores company-wide announcements, news, and updates for display on an announcement board.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Announcement entity.

content.description: The main body content of the announcement.

publishDate.description: The date and time when the announcement was published. (format: date-time)

expiryDate.description: The date and time when the announcement should no longer be displayed. Null if no expiry. (format: date-time)

authorEmployeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who authored the announcement. (Relationship: Employee 1:N Announcement)

audience.description: Specifies the intended audience for the announcement (e.g., 'All Employees', 'Team Leads').

Policy.title: Policy
Policy.description: Represents a company policy document requiring employee acknowledgment, for HR compliance.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Policy entity.

title.description: The title of the company policy (e.g., 'HR Manual', 'IT Policy').

contentUrl.description: A URL pointing to the actual policy document or content. (format: uri)

version.description: The version identifier of the policy (e.g., '1.0', '2023-Q4').

publishDate.description: The date when this version of the policy was published. (format: date)

requiredAcknowledgment.description: Indicates whether employees are required to digitally acknowledge reading this policy.

PolicyAcknowledgment.title: PolicyAcknowledgment
PolicyAcknowledgment.description: Records an employee's digital acknowledgment of having read and understood a specific company policy.

id.description: Unique identifier for the PolicyAcknowledgment entity.

employeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who acknowledged the policy. (Relationship: Employee 1:N PolicyAcknowledgment)

policyId.description: Reference to the Policy that was acknowledged. (Relationship: Policy 1:N PolicyAcknowledgment)

acknowledgmentDate.description: The date and time when the employee acknowledged the policy. (format: date-time)

ipAddress.description: The IP address from which the acknowledgment was made, for audit purposes.

AuditLog.title: AuditLog
AuditLog.description: Records all significant user actions and system events for security, compliance, and debugging purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the AuditLog entity.

timestamp.description: The date and time when the audited action occurred. (format: date-time)

employeeId.description: Reference to the Employee who performed the action. Null for system-level actions. (Relationship: Employee 1:N AuditLog)

entityType.description: The type of data entity that was affected (e.g., 'Employee', 'AttendanceRecord', 'Policy').

entityId.description: The unique identifier of the specific entity instance that was affected.

description.description: A human-readable description of the action, including context.

changes.description: A JSON string or summary describing the specific data changes made (e.g., '{"oldValue": "...", "newValue": "..."}').

ipAddress.description: The IP address from which the action was initiated.

Dedicated collection for database role-based access control (DBAC) indicating an employee is a Team Lead. Authorization based on document existence for a given employeeId (UID).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for GeoHRM is designed with a strong emphasis on Authorization Independence, Structural Segregation, and Access Modeling, as per the core design principles. The primary goal is to facilitate simple, robust, and easily debuggable security rules by minimizing `get()` calls and enabling secure `list` operations (QAPs).

**Authorization Independence via Denormalization:**
This is achieved by denormalizing crucial authorization context directly into documents where it's needed. For instance, `AttendanceRecord`, `BreakRecord`, `LeaveRequest`, and `LeaveApproval` documents, which are nested under `/employees/{employeeId}`, will include the `requestingEmployeeTeamLeadId` (the `teamLeadId` of the employee who owns the record/request). This allows a Team Lead to check if `request.auth.uid == resource.data.requestingEmployeeTeamLeadId` directly on the document being accessed, rather than needing to perform a `get()` call to the parent `/employees/{employeeId}` document to determine the owner's team lead. Similarly, `employeeId` is present in all relevant subcollection documents where an employee is the primary owner, simplifying ownership checks.

**Structural Segregation for Homogeneous Security Posture:**
Collections are designed so that all documents within a given collection share the same security requirements. For example:
*   `/system_roles_admin/{employeeId}`: Contains only UIDs of administrators, allowing rules to easily check for admin privilege via `exists()` without inspecting document content.
*   `/employees/{employeeId}/attendanceRecords/{attendanceRecordId}`: Contains only an individual employee's attendance records, accessible by the employee, their team lead, HR, or Admin. This ensures that a single set of rules can govern all documents in this subcollection.
*   Global configuration data (e.g., `/roles`, `/locations`, `/leaveTypes`, `/issueCategories`, `/policies`, `/announcements`) is placed in root collections that typically have read-only access for most employees and write access for Admin/HR.
*   Requests that require cross-role interaction (e.g., `AttendanceApprovalRequest`, `IssueReport`) are centralized in root collections to allow for efficient queries by approvers (HR/Admin) and filtered queries by requesters.

**Support for QAPs (Queries, not Filters):**
The structure supports QAPs by ensuring that any `list` operation can be secured by rules that match the query constraints. For example:
*   An employee can `list` their own attendance records (`/employees/{employeeId}/attendanceRecords`) because `employeeId` is part of the path, and rules can verify `employeeId == request.auth.uid`.
*   An Admin/HR can `list` all `AttendanceApprovalRequest` documents because they have global read access to the `/attendanceApprovalRequests` collection.
*   A Team Lead can `list` their direct reports' `LeaveRequest` documents because each `LeaveRequest` document includes the `requestingEmployeeTeamLeadId`, allowing a query like `db.collection('employees').where('requestingEmployeeTeamLeadId', '==', request.auth.uid)` to be secured by the rules which permit reads if `request.auth.uid == resource.data.requestingEmployeeTeamLeadId`.

This design minimizes complex rule logic and `get()` calls, making rules easier to write, understand, and debug, while ensuring high performance and security.
